findings.body:
**The lock retry bound is shorter than the critical section it guards.**

With `retries: 5` and `maxTimeout: 200`, a waiter gives up after about 0.5–1 s. The critical section in `resolvePrWorktree` (Line 506–678) contains `git worktree list`, per-candidate `rev-parse`/`rev-list`, `git worktree remove`, a full `git worktree add` checkout, and the caller's `onCreated` callback. On a non-trivial repository, `worktree add` alone takes longer than 1 s.

The comments at Line 473–476 describe concurrent jobs for different PRs as a supported case. In that case, the second job throws `could not acquire the registry lock … clear the stale lock and re-run`. The lock is live, not stale. Proper-lockfile keeps it fresh every `stale/2` = 5 s. The error message tells the operator to delete a lock that another process holds, and that action breaks serialization.

Size the retry budget to the expected section duration, for example tens of seconds with backoff. Also reword the error so it says the lock is held, not stale.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
       release = await lock(path, {
         stale: 10_000,
-        retries: { retries: 5, minTimeout: 25, maxTimeout: 200 },
+        // The section includes a full `worktree add` checkout; wait long enough for a live holder.
+        retries: { retries: 60, factor: 1.5, minTimeout: 100, maxTimeout: 2_000 },
         realpath: false,
       });
```
</details>
findings.title: The lock retry bound is shorter than the critical section it guards.

findings.body:
**A registered worktree whose directory is gone stops all resolution for the PR.**

Step b already handles missing directories (Line 523). Step c does not. Suppose an in-root tree carrying `cq-review/pr-<n>` is deleted with `rm -rf`. `worktree list --porcelain` still lists it, with a `prunable` line. Then:

- `rev-parse HEAD` at Line 582 fails, so `atSha` is false.
- `rev-list -C <missing>` at Line 599 fails.
- Line 601 throws "the tree's relation to the fetched head is unknown".

Every later run repeats this until someone runs `git worktree prune` by hand. Even after that throw is bypassed, `worktree add` refuses a "missing but already registered worktree".

Fix: parse the `prunable` attribute in `parseWorktreeList`. For in-root prunable candidates, run `git -C <repoRoot> worktree prune` or skip them before the unpushed-work probe. A missing directory has no work that can be orphaned.
findings.title: A registered worktree whose directory is gone stops all resolution for the PR.

findings.body:
**Derive the default `worktreeRoot` from the common git dir, not the per-worktree git dir.**

In a linked worktree, `rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` prints `<main>/.git/worktrees/<id>`, not `<main>/.git`. This causes two problems:

- The default root depends on which checkout the caller runs from. A tree created from the main checkout lands in `<main>/.git/cq-review-worktrees`. Resolution from a linked worktree uses `<main>/.git/worktrees/<id>/cq-review-worktrees`. `isInsideRoot` (Line 584) then classifies the first tree as foreign, so it is never reused or refreshed. `worktree add -B` then fails because that tree still holds the label.
- Review trees nest inside git's admin directory for the linked worktree. When `git worktree remove <linked>` or `git worktree prune` runs, git recursively deletes `.git/worktrees/<id>`. That also deletes the nested review checkouts, including any unpushed fixer work. Line 594 exists to protect that work.

The comment at Line 442 says the goal is to name "the real git dir in every layout". The common dir is the stable value for that goal. Change both derivations together so the boundary in `removePrWorktree` still matches.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-  const gitDirArgs = ['-C', repoRoot, 'rev-parse', '--absolute-git-dir'];
+  const gitDirArgs = ['-C', repoRoot, 'rev-parse', '--path-format=absolute', '--git-common-dir'];
```
Apply the same change at Line 708. `--path-format` requires git ≥ 2.31.
</details>






Also applies to: 708-718
findings.title: Derive the default `worktreeRoot` from the common git dir, not the per-worktree git dir.

findings.body:
**Make the `node_modules` refusal case-insensitive, like the `.git` check.**

Line 542 matches the segment `node_modules` exactly. A head that tracks `Node_Modules/@types/x/index.d.ts` gets past the check. On a case-insensitive filesystem (default macOS, Windows), the extracted directory then acts as `node_modules`, and `tsc` resolves head-controlled declarations. The docstring at Line 525-527 says this must be refused.

`DOT_GIT_SEGMENT` (Line 120) already handles case folding and the trailing `.`/space forms for `.git`. Apply the same handling here.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
-    if (entry.path.split('/').includes('node_modules')) {
+    if (entry.path.split('/').some((segment) => /^node_modules[. ]*$/i.test(segment))) {
```
</details>
findings.title: Make the `nodemodules` refusal case-insensitive, like the `.git` check.

findings.body:
**Validate `ref` with `assertRev` before spawning `ls-remote`.**

`gitLsRemoteRef` passes the caller's `ref` straight into the `ls-remote` pattern at Line 816. It is the only function in the module that skips the "every revision is validated BEFORE spawn" rule (Line 22). `ls-remote` arguments are glob patterns. For example, `ref = 'ma*'` matches `refs/heads/main`. If only one ref matches, the oid is returned as the pin for a ref that does not exist. `gitPushAtomic` already calls `assertRev` on its branch at Line 865.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
+  assertRev(ref, 'ls-remote');
   const { env, secrets } = gitRemoteEnv(url, token);
```
</details>
findings.title: Validate `ref` with `assertRev` before spawning `ls-remote`.
Parse only stdout in `gitLsRemoteRef`. Do not parse stdout and stderr together.

findings.body:
**Remove more environment variables that can redirect git or run programs.**

The module header (Line 16-19) says the child env drops every variable that could point git at a different config, and that nothing in ambient state can run code. `SCRUBBED_ENV` misses several variables that do this:

- `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` points git at a different global config file. `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` covers only the system config.
- `GIT_EXEC_PATH` makes git run subcommand binaries from a directory the environment chooses.
- `GIT_SSH`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` and `GIT_PROXY_COMMAND` are programs.
- `GIT_TRACE_REDACT=0` with `GIT_TRACE_CURL` or `GIT_TRACE_PACKET` writes the `AUTHORIZATION` header that `gitRemoteEnv` injects (Line 781) to a trace file.

`gitLsRemoteRef` and `gitPushAtomic` (Line 807, Line 852) carry the token through this env, so the trace case is a direct way to leak a secret.

<details>
<summary>Proposed fix</summary>

```diff
   'GIT_CONFIG',
+  'GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL',
   'GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS',
   'GIT_CONFIG_COUNT',
+  'GIT_EXEC_PATH',
+  'GIT_SSH',
+  'GIT_SSH_COMMAND',
+  'GIT_PROXY_COMMAND',
+  'GIT_TRACE_REDACT',
 ];
```
</details>
findings.title: Remove more environment variables that can redirect git or run programs.
